After Trump Media loses $360 million on Bitcoin, does the “stockpiling BTC” narrative for listed companies still hold?

Trump Media incurred a $360 million unrealized loss on crypto assets, shrinks its strategy, and the confidence of companies that focus on holding BTC has been shaken.

Trump Media (the parent company of DJT) disclosed that its losses related to digital assets amounted to $360 million, and then immediately announced a strategic adjustment, shifting its focus back to core business operations. Put simply: they “blew it” on hoarding coins, so they’re securing the main business first. This is another landmark case after some listed companies slowed their pace of buying coins— the path of configuring corporate balance sheets with BTC is starting to crack.

💡 Negative (mild).

The transmission is straightforward: listed companies reduce allocation / pause buying → the market has one less category of persistent buyers → marginal sell pressure on BTC spot increases. These buyers were previously the “second leg” after ETFs, and now one leg has weakened.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment headwind. BTC is currently at $64,321.25 (24h +1.17%). It is currently holding up on its own resilience, but the narrative that “the Trump concept is fading” will suppress risk appetite. $63,000 is the key near-term support; if it breaks, it could accelerate a pullback. ETH is at $1,902.07 (24h -0.20%), showing weaker linkage.
- Medium term: the market will be more stringent in distinguishing “real coin hoarding” (supported by cash flow) from “trend-chasing coin hoarding” (no business to back it up). Beyond the MSTR model, more imitators will find it increasingly hard to raise funding. Purging fakes and keeping the real may not be a bad thing.

One-sentence translation: The money hasn’t left BTC, but fewer listed companies are willing to stand in as a backstop for BTC.

My view
Cautious in the short term. Within the next 12 hours, BTC is likely to come under pressure and test the $63,000 support; holding it means it’s a “fake dive,” failing to hold means we’ll look at $61,500. In the medium term, however, I’m not pessimistic—when concept-driven companies exit, the remaining chips are cleaner. At this level, watching and waiting is more important than the direction itself; don’t let a single company’s earnings report scare you into panic trading.

🎯 Predicted impact

💡 Impact Assessment: Bearish in the short term; the emotional hit outweighs the actual capital flow.

Trump Media suffers a $360 million loss from digital asset holdings, shrinks its crypto strategy, and returns to its core business.

What happened?
Trump Media (the publicly listed company under Trump) took a major tumble in digital assets, posting an accounting loss of $360 million. In plain terms: the company used real money to invest in BTC and other crypto assets, but it ran into market volatility—making the financials look too ugly to explain. Now the company has announced a strategic shift: it will no longer frame Bitcoin as a core narrative, and will return to steady operations of its main business. This isn’t small change—$360 million in losses can seriously damage a media company.

One-sentence translation: The company that once rode the crypto hype has been taught a lesson by volatility, and is retreating.

Market impact
Short term: Negative on the sentiment level. The “Trump” narrative has been one of the storylines in this cycle. If his company pulls back, the market will question how much value there is in the “political endorsement.” BTC is currently at $64,321.25, up 1.17% in the past 24 hours, suggesting the news hasn’t yet caused a big shake. But if, later on, more related funds also retreat, the pressure will build. ETH is at $1,902.07, trading in a flat range.

Medium term: Actually a good thing for the industry landscape. Companies chasing hype exiting the scene suggests the market is deflating the bubble. What remains are strategic holders (for example, companies that treat BTC as a reserve asset and manage risk properly). Regulators may also use this as a case study: how high the accounting risks can be when companies “trade crypto.”

My take
In the short term, I’m bearish on sentiment; long term, I’m neutral to slightly bullish. The logic is simple: the exit of a narrative player doesn’t change the fundamental supply-demand picture. As long as BTC holds the $64,321 level, the downside support to watch is around $76.14K. If it doesn’t break, this news is just noise. A break below would be what amplifies the interpretation. As for ETH, at $1,902, it hasn’t shown real momentum—so don’t expect it to run independently. The key risk is: if more negative crypto-related actions follow from the Trump camp, the narrative could cool off more than expected.

translatedData.content:
The Protocol DevOps group of the Ethereum Platåberget Foundation launched an early test network for the Glamsterdam upgrade and opened it for community testing. According to Foresight News, the test network is expected to run for several months, providing a stable environment, with the Glamsterdam fork scheduled for August 20 on the network.

Platåberget offers a one-click network setup and a service to withdraw test ETH via its homepage. After incorporating feedback into the client program, the team plans to launch an indefinite devnet within one month to test unusual consensus scenarios. Sepolia, Hoodi, and other long-term test networks will complete the Glamsterdam fork process later before the upgrade reaches the Ethereum mainnet.

The Glamsterdam upgrade includes introducing a proposed separation between the Proposer and Builder at the system level, access lists at the block level, and re-pricing of gas fees with a minimum target of roughly 200 million gas units, as well as higher maximum sizes for initcode contracts, increasing from 24 KB and 48 KB to 64 KB and 128 KB respectively. The team said that tools relying on fixed maximum gas limits—including wallets, indexing engines, and gas estimators—will be affected and need updates.

#ETH

يقدم Platåberget إعداد شبكة بنقرة واحدة ومزودًا لسحب اختبار ETH عبر صفحته الرئيسية. بعد دمج الملاحظات في برنامج العميل، يخطط الفريق لإطلاق devnet غير نهائي خلال شهر واحد لاختبار سيناريوهات إجماع شاذة. ستكمل Sepolia وHoodi وغيرها من شبكات الاختبار طويلة الأمد لاحقًا عملية شوكة Glamsterdam قبل أن يصل الترقية إلى شبكة Ethereum الرئيسية.

يتضمن ترقية Glamsterdam إدخال فصل مُقترح المُنشئ (Proposer-Builder) على مستوى النظام، وقوائم وصول على مستوى الكتل، وإعادة تسعير رسوم الغاز مع استهداف حد أدنى يقارب 200 مليون وحدة غاز، بالإضافة إلى أحجام قصوى أعلى لعقود initcode، من 24 كيلوبايت و48 كيلوبايت إلى 64 كيلوبايت و128 كيلوبايت على التوالي. وقال الفريق إن الأدوات التي تعتمد على حدود قصوى ثابتة للغاز، بما في ذلك المحافظ ومحركات الفهرسة ومقدّري الغاز، ستتأثر وستحتاج إلى تحديثات.

title: 以太坊基金会启动 Glamsterdam 测试网：8月20日公开彩排
subTitle:
这不是又一次「测试网上线」。8 月 17 日 Platåberget 公开可加入，8 月 20 日在测试网上分叉。Fusaka 之后下一轮硬分叉，第一次让社区进来砸。很多人把这条当成又一次「测试网上线」。错了。
8 月 17 日，以太坊基金会 Protocol DevOps 宣布：Glamsterdam 的早期公开测试网 Platåberget 已上线。 8 月 20 日，这条测试网会真正分叉。
这不是 devnet 关起门来打补丁。这是 Fusaka 之后下一轮硬分叉，第一次让社区进来砸。
先看现货：
· 币安 ETH 约 $1,895，24h -0.1% · 距 ATH 约 -61% · 近 1 年约 -56%
价格还在腰斩区间。升级很硬，盘面还没给它定价。

一、先把路径看清楚：测试网 ≠ 主网

官方路径写得很死：
· 8/17 上线 Platåberget（公开可加入） · 8/20 在测试网上激活 Glamsterdam · 跑几个月，让钱包、节点、DVT、solo 质押把东西打爆 · 稳定后再上长寿命测试网 Sepolia / Hoodi · 最后才是主网
名字也不是乱取的：Glamsterdam = Gloas（共识层）+ Amsterdam（执行层）。两边必须一起升。只升一个，链会裂。
持有现货 ETH 的人：什么都不用做。 跑节点、做质押、写钱包、估 Gas 的人：现在就该去测试网。

二、四个硬改动：出块和执行一起换引擎

ePBS（EIP-7732） 出块权写进协议。今天超过八成区块走链下 MEV-Boost 中继，靠信任。Glamsterdam 要把 builder 变成协议里的一等公民，并加上 PTC（payload 是否按时送达）检查。BAL（EIP-7928） 区块级访问列表。一个块碰过哪些账户、哪些存储槽，提前记下来。这是并行执行的预声明，不是装饰。Gas 重定价 目标是大约 2 亿 Gas 下限。任何硬编码「最大 Gas」的钱包、索引器、估算器，都会坏。更狠的一句：普通转账也不再永远是 21000。转到已存在地址仍是 21000；转到全新空地址，还要额外付「状态字节」费用。更大合约 合约上限 24 KiB → 64 KiB initcode 48 KiB → 128 KiB

三、真正的赌注：L1 吞吐从 60M 推向 200M

当前 Gas 下限大约 6000 万。Glamsterdam 的工作目标大约 2 亿。3.3 倍。
这不是「Gas 会立刻变便宜」的口号。这是 L1 把扩容叙事从「全靠 L2」往回抢一点。
Fusaka 解决数据可用性。Glamsterdam 解决出块管道 + 执行引擎。下一轮 Hegotá（大约 2027）才轮到 FOCIL 抗审查。
所以别问「ETH 会不会因此暴拉」。该问的是：2 亿 Gas 这条路，测试网能不能走通。

四、价格还在腰斩：升级是中期催化剂，不是今日情绪

ETH 近一年大约 -56%，距高点大约 -61%。现价在 $1,895 附近磨。
测试网上线通常不会当天改定价。但它改的是 2026 下半年的叙事：
· 主网日期还没锁，更现实的窗口是 Q4 · 先看 8/20 分叉顺不顺 · 再看钱包 / RPC / 估算器有没有大面积报错 · 最后才轮到 Sepolia、Hoodi、主网

五、三类人，三件事
只持有 ETH：不用操作。这不是需要迁币的分叉。节点 / 质押 / 建设者：去 Platåberget 存验证者、走 builder 流程。ePBS 是共识层大改，关起门测不够。钱包 / dApp / 索引器：立刻丢掉「最大 Gas 写死」和「转账永远 21000」这两条假设。官方点名：这类工具最容易在主网那天集体出事。

我的判断（非投资建议）：
· 8/20 测试网分叉，是 Glamsterdam 的第一道公开考 · 对价格是中期叙事，不是 24 小时情绪 · ETH 仍在腰斩区间，升级成功会给 L1 估值一个新锚，失败则继续磨
你是觉得 2 亿 Gas 会让 ETH 重新被写成「L1 还能自己扩」，还是觉得这轮还是 L2 的戏，主网只是换了出块管道？

translatedData.subTitle:
This isn’t another “testnet launch.” On August 17, Platåberget becomes publicly joinable; on August 20, it will fork on the testnet. The next round of a hard fork after Fusaka is the first time the community is allowed to come in and hammer at it. Many people are treating this as another “testnet launch.” They’re wrong.
On August 17, the Ethereum Foundation Protocol DevOps announced that Platåberget, the early public testnet for Glamsterdam, has gone live. On August 20, this testnet will truly fork.
This isn’t a devnet, patching behind closed doors. This is the next round of a hard fork after Fusaka, the first time the community gets to come in and take a crack at it.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Talking about Dusk—embedding the privacy components and the Citadel KYC protocol directly into the underlying architecture—has consistently drawn high praise within the industry. Objectively speaking, this approach is truly cutting-edge: without relying on external application-layer plugins, it natively embeds PLONK zk-SNARKs and Bulletproofs directly at the chain-level network layer. Then add Citadel’s identity system: players only need to present a “regulator-compliant” cryptographic verification result, without even having to transmit passport photocopies. This move really strikes the right balance between data concealment and financial compliance.

But when I finally read through the audit drafts provided by those security experts, I felt a chill down my spine. The PLONK implementation vulnerability caught by the OtterSec team essentially tests the very limits of public-chain security. The underlying principle isn’t complicated: at the core verification node, when checking the final mathematical constraints, it actually takes the four evaluation results of the prover’s selection polynomials and uses them directly—completely skipping the crucial KZG commitment opening verification. Put simply, it’s like an inspection machine has been plugged in but never switched on. If a hacker follows the trail, they can arbitrarily tamper with these parameters, bypass the verification rules, generate DUSK out of thin air, and then use the normal Phoenix mechanism to move the counterfeit tokens out successfully.

What’s most hard to believe is that this chain’s privacy system serves as the backstop for roughly a $DUSK pool of nearly $60 million. With an asset of that scale, the lifeline of its security ends up hinging on the absence of a basic verification step. Even more absurdly, this deadly unlimited-minting bug managed to survive for over two years in plain sight of major top-tier security organizations, going through multiple rounds of reviews yet never being caught. Although the dusk-plonk module has now patched the issue, once something like this happens, the bottom line has already been breached.

The infrastructure fuses cryptographic primitives at the base level, and the original intent is obviously to be truly one-and-done. But the big prerequisite is that your code must fit together with mathematical precision—tight and seamless. A ZK network that can make such a glaring mistake even in a basic verification engine: when Citadel issues identity proofs in the future, who can guarantee they won’t be mass-forged by gray-market actors? In reality, haven’t we also buried deeper risks that could instantly destroy the entire ecosystem? This score is worth recalculating for everyone.#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Recently, I’ve been studying Dusk—the idea of directly weaving zero-knowledge proofs and Citadel KYC into the base layer of a public blockchain. After reading through it, I’m honestly left with a mix of feelings.

You have to admit, in the privacy space, this architecture is incredibly ambitious. Most projects simply bolt a privacy plugin onto the application layer, but Dusk goes another route: it hardwires PLONK zk-SNARKs and Bulletproofs into the Layer 1 foundation itself. Then, paired with Citadel’s identity protocol, users only need to provide a cryptographic credential proving they’re “qualified,” without uploading their passport’s real-name information. From the concept alone, it’s certainly a strong hand for solving both “data concealment” and “regulatory compliance.”

But after going through the latest code audit report, I literally took a breath and felt my heart sink.

The security team, OtterSec, found a flaw in Dusk’s PLONK core library that is arguably fatal. In simple terms, when the verification node runs the final equation, it blindly trusts four selector parameters submitted by the prover—somehow it even omitted the most critical KZG opening verification step. What does that mean? It’s like a security guard checking tickets: they just ask, “Do you have a ticket?” and when the person says “yes,” the guard lets them in without ever verifying whether the ticket is genuine. With this boundary-defeating weakness, malicious actors could freely fabricate data, printing countless DUSK out of thin air, and then openly wash and cash in the fake coins by following the Phoenix transaction path.

You should know that this privacy chain carries a market value as high as $DUSK 60 million. For a fund pool that enormous, its survival—or demise—ends up hinging on a single commonly skipped validation step. Even more surreal is that this “time bomb” in the code has gone through multiple rounds of audits by different institutions over the past two years, yet it somehow never got defused. Sure, the official team later rushed to patch the dusk-plonk module, but the underlying risk is still unsettling and hard to sleep easy over.

Embedding cryptographic components deep into the base layer is, in theory, more of a one-and-done solution than outsourcing to a DApp. But it demands absolute rigor from the infrastructure. By binding ZK deeply to the root of a public chain, are you building a stronger firewall—or, without realizing it, planting a landmine with even greater destructive power? This is something people in the industry should think through carefully.#eth $ETH

U.S. 30-year Treasury yield rises to a near-20-year high

In recent times, volatility in the U.S. Treasury market has increased. Long-end yields have continued to come under pressure and move higher, becoming an important macro variable in cross-asset pricing. Market attention has shifted from the path of short-term policy rates to a broader set of factors, including fiscal supply, inflation stickiness, and the supply-demand structure of long-dated bonds—making the trajectory of ultra-long-end yields even more signal-relevant.

On the key facts side, related reports indicate that the yield on U.S. 30-year Treasuries climbed to 5.29%, the highest since 2007. Contributing factors include investors’ concerns about the expansion of U.S. debt, a surge in Treasury issuance, and inflation remaining relatively high. Increased debt financing by AI-related companies, along with weaker demand for long-dated Treasuries, has also marginally added to pressure on the long end. Although data on employment, inflation, and retail sales have been somewhat weak, leading the market to scale back expectations for near-term rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, the selling of U.S. Treasuries has continued. With long-end yields rising and short-end yields falling, the yield curve has steepened. Earlier, the primary market also sent similar pressure signals: the U.S. Treasury completed a $42 billion 10-year Treasury auction, with a winning yield of 4.683%, the highest since the global financial crisis in 2007. At that time, the market also expected that the subsequent 30-year auction might face even higher funding rates. Inflation staying above the policy target and the widening fiscal deficit have been cited as the main backdrop for suppressing long-dated bond prices and pushing up long-term yields.

Breaking down the logic, long-end yields are not determined solely by expectations for near-term rate hikes or cuts; they depend more on the term premium, net supply size, and the medium-term outlook for growth and inflation. When primary issuance remains persistently heavy and secondaries show insufficient willingness to absorb longer-duration risk, investors demand higher coupon compensation for holding risk. If core inflation declines more slowly than expected, the attractiveness of real bond returns falls, making it easier for the yield “center” to move higher. Short-end yields have relatively fallen due to weaker recent data and reduced urgency for near-month rate hikes, while the long end moves up—together resulting in a steepening curve. This more closely resembles the market simultaneously pricing “easing pressure from near-end policy” and “rising uncertainty about fiscal and inflation conditions at the far end,” rather than a single-direction narrative of easing or tightening.

Regarding the impact on crypto assets, it is better to understand it through transmission channels involving liquidity and risk appetite—not through a simple one-to-one mapping of up/down moves. A rise in long-end U.S. Treasury yields typically implies higher discount rates for global risk assets, which may suppress the relative appeal of long-duration, high-volatility instruments. If this process is accompanied by higher real yields or expectations of tighter U.S. dollar liquidity, crypto market volatility could also be amplified. On the other hand, if investors interpret the curve’s steepening as evidence that growth resilience remains and policy does not need to be excessively tightened, risk appetite may sometimes repair in phases. These pathways are influenced jointly by the U.S. dollar trend, real yields, leverage levels, and market crowding. This is probabilistic transmission; it’s not appropriate to extrapolate a crypto market direction directly from a single yield level. On the factual side, attention should be anchored to debt supply, auction demand, and inflation/employment data; on the speculative side, multiple scenarios should remain on the table.

The editorial view is that the crucial issue now is not the level of yields on any single trading day. Instead, it is whether the high yields can be digested by the market, whether the Treasury’s subsequent issuance pace will continue to strain supply-demand dynamics, and whether the slope of inflation’s decline is steep enough to compress the term premium. Upcoming key central bank communication windows may also reshape how the market understands the policy reaction function. For participants in crypto markets, a more prudent approach is to view volatility in long-end U.S. Treasuries as a change in pricing constraint conditions: distinguish verified macro facts from short-term sentiment-driven narratives, and focus on the linkage between liquidity and risk premia rather than simplifying a complex rate structure into a one-way trading story.

美国三十年期国债收益率升至近二十年高位

近期美国国债市场波动升温，长端利率持续承压上行，成为跨资产定价的重要宏观变量。市场关注点从短期政策利率路径，进一步扩展到财政供给、通胀粘性与长久期债券供需结构，使超长端收益率走势更具信号意义。

核心事实方面，相关报道显示，美国30年期国债收益率攀升至5.29%，创下2007年以来新高。推动因素包括投资者对美国债务规模膨胀、国债发行放量以及通胀仍然偏高的担忧。人工智能相关企业举债融资增加，叠加长期债券需求走弱，也在边际上加大长端压力。尽管就业、通胀与零售等数据表现偏弱，市场相应下调了对美联储短期加息的预期，但美债抛售仍在延续；长端收益率上行、短端收益率回落，收益率曲线呈现陡峭化。稍早前的一级市场亦释放类似压力信号：美国财政部完成420亿美元10年期国债拍卖，中标收益率达4.683%，为2007年全球金融危机以来最高；当时市场亦预期随后的30年期拍卖可能面对更高融资利率。通胀持续高于政策目标、财政赤字扩大，被指是压制长端债券价格、推升长期收益率的主要背景。

从逻辑上拆解，长端收益率并不只由短期加息或降息预期决定，更取决于期限溢价、净供给规模、增长与通胀的中期判断。当一级供给持续偏大、二级市场长久期承接意愿不足时，投资者会要求更高票息补偿持有风险；若核心通胀回落偏慢，债券实际回报吸引力下降，收益率中枢更容易上移。短端因近期数据偏弱、近月加息紧迫性下降而相对回落，与长端上行并存，就会表现为曲线陡峭化。这更像是市场在同时交易“近端政策压力缓和”和“远端财政与通胀不确定性抬升”，而不是单一方向的宽松或紧缩叙事。

对加密资产的影响，更宜放在流动性与风险偏好的传导路径中理解，而非简单对应涨跌。长端美债收益率上行，通常意味着全球风险资产折现率抬升，长久期、高波动品种的相对吸引力可能受到抑制；若过程伴随实际利率走高或美元流动性收紧预期，加密市场波动也可能被放大。另一方面，若曲线陡峭化被部分资金解读为增长韧性仍在、政策无需过度紧缩，风险偏好有时也能阶段性修复。上述路径受美元走势、实际利率、杠杆水平与市场拥挤度共同影响，属于或然传导，不能把单一收益率点位直接外推为加密行情方向。事实层面应锚定债务供给、拍卖需求与通胀就业数据，推测层面则需保留多种情景。

编辑判断是，当前关键不在于某一交易日的点位本身，而在于高位收益率能否被市场消化、财政部后续发行节奏是否继续冲击供需，以及通胀回落斜率是否足以压低期限溢价。临近的重要央行沟通窗口也可能改变市场对政策反应函数的理解。对加密市场参与者而言，更稳妥的做法是把美债长端波动视为定价约束条件的变化，区分已验证的宏观事实与短期情绪推演，关注流动性与风险溢价的联动，而不是把复杂利率结构简化成单向交易故事。

⚠️ ETH DEVELOPERS: GLAMSTERDAM COULD BREAK SOME TOOLS 💀

The Ethereum Foundation warns that the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade may cause some wallets, indexing tools, and gas estimators to behave abnormally.

The issue lies in the change to the gas model. According to the EF, tools that hard-code the maximum gas limit may no longer work correctly and need to be updated.

Glamsterdam is expected to activate on 20/8, then roll out to the Sepolia and Hoodi testnets.

Notably, EIP-8037 will add a separate gas space for state. Transferring ETH to an existing account still costs 21,000 gas, but transferring to a new account will incur additional state gas.

I think this is the kind of upgrade that ordinary users can hardly notice, but developer tooling could get hit first.

ETH: “Big upgrade incoming.”

If you’re using Ethereum-related wallets/tooling, this is the time for devs to test and update before the upgrade goes live.

title: 🚨Ethereum Glamsterdam Delayed: Could This Upgrade Still Send ETH Toward $2,000?
subTitle:
Ethereum just entered a major new testing phase — but there is a twist. Glamsterdam is now targeted for Q4 2026, while the new Platåberget public testnet is already open for testing.

For ETH traders, this is a much bigger story than a simple upgrade delay.

Ethereum is preparing one of its most important protocol changes since The Merge, with Glamsterdam designed to improve Layer 1 capacity, enable more parallel processing and change how blocks are built. At the same time, the Ethereum Foundation has warned that some wallets, indexers and gas-estimation tools could break if they rely on old gas assumptions.

So the question for traders is:

Can Glamsterdam become the catalyst that finally pushes ETH toward $2,000 — or will the delay keep bulls waiting?

🔥 What Just Happened?

On August 17, the Ethereum Foundation announced the launch of Platåberget, a public testnet created specifically to test Glamsterdam.

This is important because developers now have a broader environment where clients, validators, infrastructure providers and application developers can test the upcoming changes before the upgrade eventually reaches mainnet.

But there is also a timeline change.

Ethereum's official roadmap now lists Glamsterdam for Q4 2026, rather than an earlier 2026 target.

For investors, that creates both a positive and a negative interpretation.

The negative side is obvious:

The upgrade is taking longer.

But the positive side is arguably more important:

Ethereum developers are giving the upgrade more time for testing before putting billions of dollars of economic activity behind it.

🧊 Why Is Glamsterdam So Important?

Glamsterdam combines changes to Ethereum's execution and consensus layers.

Two of the headline components are:

ePBS — Enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation

and

BALs — Block-Level Access Lists.

ePBS is designed to bring proposer-builder separation directly into Ethereum's protocol, while BALs are intended to provide a foundation for more parallel transaction execution.

In simple words:

Ethereum wants to process more activity while improving the way blocks are constructed and validated.

That could become increasingly important as decentralized finance, stablecoins, tokenized assets and Layer 2 networks continue to grow.

⚡ The Big Gas-Model Change

One of the most interesting parts of the current testnet is the change to Ethereum's gas model.

The Ethereum Foundation warned that EIP-8037 introduces a new state-gas charge, meaning certain operations that create new state could cost more than users are accustomed to paying today.

This may sound like a technical developer issue.

It isn't.

Wallets and infrastructure tools often depend on assumptions about gas limits and transaction costs.

If those assumptions become outdated, applications may behave incorrectly.

That is why Ethereum's team is warning developers early.

The goal is to discover these problems on the testnet rather than after mainnet activation.

⚠️ Could Wallets Actually Break?

The Ethereum Foundation has specifically warned that tools relying on a hard-capped maximum gas limit — including some wallets, indexers and gas estimators — may need updates.

This does not mean that ordinary ETH holders need to panic.

It also does not mean users need to transfer their ETH or perform a token migration.

Glamsterdam is a protocol upgrade, not a new ETH token.

The main responsibility falls on developers, infrastructure providers, validators and service operators to make sure their software is compatible before mainnet activation.

📈 Why Could This Be Bullish for ETH?

Ethereum's long-term challenge is simple:

Can the network scale while maintaining security and decentralization?

Glamsterdam is aimed directly at that problem.

If the upgrade successfully improves execution efficiency and Layer 1 capacity, it could strengthen Ethereum's position as infrastructure for DeFi, stablecoins, tokenized real-world assets and Layer 2 ecosystems.

That could eventually create a stronger fundamental narrative for ETH.

And crypto markets love narratives.

When traders see:

Major upgrade + improved scalability + institutional adoption + strong ecosystem

sentiment can change quickly.

🎯 Could ETH Reach $2,000?

This is where traders need to separate fundamentals from price predictions.

Glamsterdam alone cannot guarantee that ETH will reach $2,000.

ETH still depends on Bitcoin, macroeconomic conditions, liquidity, ETF flows and overall crypto-market sentiment.

But the upgrade could become an important catalyst if ETH is already showing strong momentum.

A bullish roadmap could look like:

$1,900 → $2,000 → $2,100 → $2,200

The $2,000 level would be especially important because psychological round numbers often attract both buyers and sellers.

A clean breakout above $2,000 with strong volume would be much more meaningful than a temporary spike above the level.

🟢 Bullish Scenario

The bullish setup is straightforward.

If ETH continues holding its nearby support levels, market sentiment improves and Ethereum's upgrade narrative gains attention, buyers could attempt to push ETH higher.

A strong move above the current resistance structure could bring $2,000 back into focus.

If ETH breaks $2,000 and successfully turns it into support, traders could start watching higher targets.

The strongest version of this scenario would combine:

ETH breakout + rising volume + improving ETF flows + positive crypto sentiment + successful Glamsterdam testing.

That combination could be powerful.

🔴 Bearish Scenario

There is also a clear risk.

If ETH fails to hold support while Bitcoin remains weak, the Glamsterdam story may not be enough to stop sellers.

A delayed upgrade can also become a short-term negative headline if traders focus only on the postponement.

The market could interpret:

“Q4 2026 target”

as another delay rather than evidence of careful testing.

This is why price action remains more important than the headline.

A great upgrade does not automatically produce a rally if the broader market is bearish.

🐋 Why Whales and Institutions Matter

Ethereum's future is increasingly connected to institutional adoption.

Large investors are looking at ETH not simply as a cryptocurrency but as exposure to an ecosystem containing DeFi, stablecoins, tokenization and smart-contract infrastructure.

If institutional demand strengthens while Ethereum's protocol becomes more scalable, the long-term investment narrative could become stronger.

This is why Glamsterdam matters beyond technical developers.

It could influence how investors think about Ethereum's competitiveness over the next several years.

🌐 Ethereum vs. Other Smart-Contract Networks

Ethereum is not operating in a vacuum.

Solana and other high-performance networks continue competing for developers, users and liquidity.

Ethereum's biggest advantage remains its enormous ecosystem and developer base.

But competitors are constantly pushing transaction speed, fees and user experience.

Glamsterdam is therefore partly about keeping Ethereum competitive.

The goal is not simply to make Ethereum faster.

It is to improve the base layer while preserving the network's broader security and decentralization goals.

👀 What Traders Should Watch

For ETH traders, there are several things worth monitoring.

1. Glamsterdam Testing

The Platåberget testnet will provide important information about how the upgrade behaves under real testing conditions.

2. Developer Warnings

If more compatibility issues appear, the mainnet timeline could potentially move again.

3. ETH Price Structure

Watch whether ETH can reclaim important psychological resistance levels.

4. ETH ETF Flows

Institutional flows can provide an important indication of demand.

5. Bitcoin

ETH rarely trades completely independently from $BTC .

If Bitcoin enters a strong rally, Ethereum could benefit from broader market liquidity.

🚨 The Delay May Actually Be Bullish

Here is the controversial part.

Some traders may see the Q4 2026 target as bearish.

But from a network-development perspective, delaying a major protocol upgrade can be positive if the extra time reduces technical risk.

Ethereum's public testnet process is designed to uncover problems before mainnet.

The Ethereum Foundation explicitly described Platåberget as an early opportunity for developers to test breaking changes.

In other words:

A slower upgrade could potentially mean a safer upgrade.

For a blockchain securing billions of dollars, that matters.

🔮 Final Outlook

Ethereum has just entered another important chapter.

Glamsterdam is no longer simply an upcoming upgrade on a roadmap.

The Platåberget public testnet is now live, developers are testing major changes, and the mainnet target has shifted toward Q4 2026.

The upgrade brings major technical changes involving block production, access lists and gas economics.

It also creates short-term risks because some existing infrastructure may need updates.

For ETH investors, the most important question is whether these technical improvements eventually translate into stronger network usage and greater investor confidence.

If testing goes smoothly, Ethereum could enter the next stage of its scaling roadmap with a much stronger foundation.

And if the broader crypto market turns bullish at the same time?

ETH could have a very interesting road ahead.

🔥 The big question: Will Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade become the catalyst for ETH to reclaim $2,000 — or will the Q4 delay keep bulls waiting?

After the ONE cross-chain bridge was hacked, Harmony decided to roll the chain back: erasing 109,000 transactions—still decentralized?

Harmony plans to roll back 109,000 transactions to patch the ONE vulnerability, challenging the line of “code is law.”

In 2022, the ONE cross-chain bridge was hacked, with losses of about $100 million. Now the Harmony team proposes a solution: directly roll back the chain, delete the 109,000 transactions after the attack occurred, and restore the state to before the hack. The rationale is that “selectively restoring transactions would cause the blockchain state to become inconsistent,” and technically it’s impossible to revoke only the stolen transaction. Similar to this, the Ravencoin community is also in uproar over a rollback dispute. In short, both chains face the same existential test: when something goes wrong, do you own up, or do you change the ledger?

One-sentence translation: When a decentralized chain most needs to prove it can’t be tampered with, it presses the restart button.

Market impact
- Short term: This is negative sentiment for an older coin, and has limited impact on the broader trading of BTC and ETH. BTC is currently $64,256.75 (24h +1.36%), ETH is $1,899.11 (24h +0.21%). The overall market is moving on its own rhythm; these kinds of chain-level controversies usually only dampen their own token sentiment.
- Medium term: The real issue is at the industry narrative level. If rollbacks become a “standard procedure” after hacks, the core value proposition of a public chain being “immutable” is effectively discounted. What regulators and institutions care about most is precisely this. Bridge security has long been an old sore spot—this news is essentially adding salt to the wound.

My take
I’ll mainly observe, but my view is clear: for ONE, this is a long-term credit negative. It doesn’t create any material bearish impact on BTC or ETH. As long as BTC holds above $64,000, the short-term structure isn’t broken; ETH is ranging around $1,900, and this news has nothing to do with it. What you should really be wary of is this: if the small-cap public chain you hold has a precedent for rollback, then next time something happens, it will most likely do the same. Risk premium for such assets should be higher. Don’t treat “the team will save the chain” as a positive—that’s precisely evidence of centralization.

After Harmony was hacked, it plans to roll back 109,000 transactions: blockchain immutability—how much is left?

Harmony is preparing to roll back on-chain data to fix the vulnerability, wiping 109,000 transaction records in one go.

After suffering an ONE token vulnerability attack, the official solution from Harmony is to roll back the entire chain, not to selectively restore transactions. The reason is technical: restoring only part of the transactions would make the chain state inconsistent, so the ledger wouldn’t match. So they chose a clean cut—those 109,000 transactions are effectively void and the ledger is rewritten. Coincidentally, Ravencoin just disclosed a vulnerability as well, facing a similar debate over whether to roll back. The two chains nearly hit the same dilemma at almost the same time: whether to tamper with historical data.

One-sentence translation: To recover the hacker’s money, the project team chose to rewrite the ledger—which in traditional finance is called “a bank changing the transaction flow,” and in blockchain it used to be “impossible.”

Impact on the market
- Short term: Splits within the ONE community are inevitable, and holders’ trust in the project will take a hit. This kind of news has limited impact on mainstream coins like BTC and ETH. Currently, BTC is around $64,256 and ETH around $1,899, with volatility staying within normal ranges. What’s truly affected is the overall reputation premium of smaller mid-to-low-cap chains.
- Medium term: This sets a dangerous precedent. If rollbacks become the standard response after a vulnerability, then “immutability” becomes “immutability, unless something goes wrong.” When institutions do due diligence, they’ll factor this risk into pricing, and the valuation logic for public chains will need to be rewritten.

My take
My view: I’m bearish on Harmony and similar public chains that have the power to roll back history. This isn’t a technical issue—it’s a trust issue. BTC’s core value is precisely that it has never rolled back transactions. Even the overflow vulnerability fix in 2010 didn’t touch user balances. This event, in fact, reinforces BTC’s scarcity narrative. ETH went through the 2016 DAO fork, and old players still remember how ETC came about—communities are extremely sensitive to the word “rollback.” ONE faces mid-term pressure, while BTC relatively benefits from the comparison effect.

Risk point: If more chains follow the rollback playbook, regulatory scrutiny across the whole industry will intensify.

- Coin: BTC / ETH
- Direction: Bearish 📉 Predict a drop
- Duration: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours

content:
Harmony被黑后要回滚10.9万笔交易：区块链的不可篡改，到底还剩多少

Harmony为修复漏洞准备回滚链上数据，一次性抹掉10.9万笔交易记录。

Harmony在遭遇ONE代币漏洞攻击后，官方给出的方案是整体回滚，而不是选择性恢复交易。理由很技术：只恢复部分交易会导致链状态不一致，账本对不上。所以干脆一刀切，10.9万笔交易直接作废重写。更巧的是，Ravencoin那边也刚出过漏洞，也面临是否回滚的争议。两条链几乎同时撞上“要不要动历史数据”这道选择题。

一句话翻译：为了追回黑客的钱，项目方选择重写账本——这在传统金融叫银行改流水，在区块链曾经叫不可能。

对市场的影响
- 短期：ONE社区内部分裂难免，持币者对项目方信任打折。这种消息对BTC、ETH这类主流币影响有限，当前BTC在$64,256附近、ETH在$1,899，波动都在正常区间。真正被打击的是中小公链的整体信誉溢价。
- 中期：这开了个危险的口子。如果回滚成为漏洞后的标准操作，“不可篡改”就变成了“不可篡改，除非出事”。机构做尽调时会把这个风险计入定价，公链估值逻辑要重写。

我的判断
我的看法：对Harmony及类似有权回滚历史的公链偏空，这不是技术问题，是信任问题。BTC的核心价值恰恰在于它从没回滚过交易——2010年那次溢出漏洞修复都没动用户余额。这次事件反而强化BTC的稀缺叙事。ETH经历过2016年DAO分叉，老玩家都记得ETC怎么来的，社区对“回滚”两个字极其敏感。ONE这类币中期承压，BTC则相对受益于对比效应。风险点：如果更多链效仿回滚，整个行业监管审视会加码。

Oil prices are up 30%. Trump blames Iran—and this is actually a bad signal for Bitcoin

U.S. oil prices have surged 30%, bringing inflation pressure back. That makes it even harder for the Federal Reserve to cut rates, which is a direct, real bearish factor for BTC.

Trump directly attributes the oil price increase to the Iran conflict. Geopolitical tensions push up energy prices. A move of 30% is not small—remember, oil prices are an important component of CPI. With gasoline jumping this hard, inflation data over the next few months will likely look ugly. For the crypto market, this isn’t some far-off story—it’s real pressure that directly affects the Federal Reserve’s policy path. BTC is currently around $64,211.82, up only 1.27% over the past 24 hours. This kind of rebound on shrinking volume is, by itself, not “real.”

Market impact
- Short term: Inflation expectations heat up → rate-cut expectations get delayed → risk assets come under pressure. At the $64,211.82 level, BTC has no incremental inflow of funds; the rebound is driven by existing positioning. ETH is at $1,898.01, up just 0.19% over 24 hours—so it’s weaker than BTC.
- Medium term: If oil prices keep staying elevated, energy-driven inflation will repeatedly disrupt CPI, throwing off the Fed’s easing rhythm. But liquidity is the fundamental logic behind bull and bear cycles in crypto. Once that logic wavers, medium-term valuations have to be marked down.

My view
I’m bearish in the short term. The logic is straightforward: a 30% oil price jump first feeds into inflation expectations, then into interest rate expectations, and finally hits risk appetite. Around $66K above is the resistance zone; $62K below is short-term support. If it breaks, it could accelerate the move to test lower levels. ETH is relatively weaker; the rebound strength is even less than BTC’s. Don’t count on it to independently strengthen.

【Monad doesn’t let people leave—this is scarier than you think】

Have you seen the news? There’s a project called Monad that recently did something pretty against common sense—giving early investors a free $60 million so they leave right now.

What would normal people react with? “Is this project crazy? Giving away money to make people run?”

But think about it carefully: between paying people to leave and going straight to listing that makes investors dump—what hurts the token price more?

The answer is obvious.

So Monad’s move, translated into one sentence, is: I know I’m not ready to let you all out yet. If I do, you’ll dump the market, and I can’t control it.

This isn’t generosity. It’s market support. The very act of “supporting the market” itself proves that—right now, the secondary market can’t even absorb this amount.

Now look at ETH. The FNG index is 41, and the weekly average is only 32—higher than average, but nowhere near euphoria. Sounds pretty safe, doesn’t it?

But the issue was never whether it’s crazy right now. The real question is—

What position are you in right now?

I’ve seen too many people. Every time someone says, “I’ll just try with a small position.” And then what happens? You try—and you’re gone.

The muscle memory from 2021 tells me: at this level, on paper it looks undervalued. But being undervalued doesn’t mean it has to go up. It doesn’t mean you can go heavy. And it definitely doesn’t mean you can throw your risk management playbook away.

Bitmine is still scooping up. That 5% of ETH is nearly being taken up by them alone. Unrealized losses are $8.4 billion—sounds terrifying on paper, right? But they just keep buying.

Do you follow this kind of “irrational” behavior?

If you follow, you’re betting it’s right.

If you don’t, you’re betting it’s wrong.

But the market never plays your game. It only exists to make you regret it.

So I’ll ask you one last thing—

Have you hedged right now? Or are you going all-in, waiting for a break-even to save you?

content:
【Monad不让人走，这事比你想的更吓人】

你们看新闻了吗？有个叫Monad的项目，最近干了件挺反常识的事——给早期投资人白送6000万美元，让他们现在就走。

正常人什么反应？“这项目疯了？送钱让人跑？”

但你仔细想想，送钱让人走，和直接上市让投资人砸盘，哪个对代币价格伤害大？

答案很明显。

所以Monad这波操作，翻译过来就一句话：我知道自己还没准备好让你们出来，出来就是砸盘，我压不住。

这不是大方，这是护盘。护盘这件事本身，就说明了——现在二级市场根本接不住这个量。

你再看看ETH这边。FNG指数41，周均才32，比平均高出不少，但远没到狂热的时候。听起来好像还挺安全？

但问题从来不是现在疯没疯。问题是——

你看看自己现在什么仓位？

我见过太多人了，每次说“我就小仓位试试”，结果呢？试试就逝世。2021年的肌肉记忆告诉我，现在这个位置，账面看好像低估了，但低估不代表要涨，不代表可以重仓，不代表你可以把风险管理手册扔了。

Bitmine还在扫货，5%的ETH快被它一家包圆了。未实现亏损84亿美元，账面看着吓人吧？但人家就是不停买。

To be honest, what gets me most worked up about this chart isn’t the up or down—it’s that kind of tug-of-war where it looks like there’s a chance, but the moment you jump in, it just fizzles out. Bitcoin is still grinding around the 63k area; you think it’s about to break out with volume, and then it pulls back again. The most punishing part of this kind of market isn’t the direction—it’s the fact that you can’t help but make a move. My simple workaround is just one line: I won’t chase a breakout unless it comes with volume—let the dust settle first.

Honestly, lately everyone’s been shifting their focus back and forth among a few hot themes in the order book. AI coins and memes—things with big volatility—are indeed lively, but you’re only meant to play them when there’s liquidity. Without volume, if you chase in, you’re basically lifting someone else’s seat. I personally only watch one thing—whether capital is genuinely flowing in. If you look at Bitcoin, it’s even bouncing around in a range; the majors haven’t given any clear direction. Most of the moves in small caps are probably just circulating stock among existing funds—if they can’t hold the liquidity, you end up in deep water.

As for the contracts, I need to nag about it too. In a market that’s stuck in this awkward in-between state, what you fear most isn’t being wrong on the view—it’s adding size to try to get your money back, or obsessing over grinding your way with fees. Let me say it plainly: fees don’t look like much. You can burn away a few hundred U in a day and not even realize where the money went. Before opening a position, ask yourself: if this trade gets swept, do I accept it? If you don’t, don’t open.

Anyway, my rhythm is this: stay light on the majors, only sip from the hot themes, and don’t go heavy betting on direction. Not being able to take the last penny isn’t embarrassing—getting dragged by the market because you can’t control yourself is. Tether is bringing AI tools to emerging markets: this time it’s not about reserves, but technology

💡 Positive, neutral-to-warm sentiment. The main upside is for the BNB ecosystem and the stablecoin sector.

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino has said they will bring foundational AI tools to emerging markets, backed by a solid audit report.

In one sentence
Tether’s entry into AI means the stablecoin competition shifts from “who is trustworthy” to “who is more useful.”

What’s going on
Ardoino’s wording is very direct: Tether plans to roll out foundational AI tools in emerging markets. Users in these regions don’t lack USD-pegged stablecoins—they lack affordable, practical, localized services, like translation, payments, and communications—real day-to-day necessities. Tether already has USDT as a distribution channel, and its penetration in Africa, Southeast Asia, and Latin America has long been among the strongest on the planet. Now while BTC is trading sideways around $64,230 and ETH is grinding at $1,899, the valuation logic in the stablecoin space is quietly changing its anchor: shifting from audit transparency to technical capability. The original statement makes it clear— the competitive focus is moving from trust to technological innovation.

One-sentence translation: USDT isn’t just becoming a “digital dollar.” Tether wants to be the underlying operating system for emerging markets.

Market impact
- Short term: A sentiment tailwind. Every time Tether makes a big move, it brings traffic, and BNB—being the main settlement chain for stablecoins—benefits most directly. BTC will likely keep ranging near $64,230, so the direct catalyst is limited.
- Medium term: Industry dynamics will change. Circle and Binance are competing over stablecoin added features, and AI is the next battleground. Emerging markets mean the next wave of user growth—whoever gets in first captures the upside. Regulators may even feel more at ease: AI expansion with audit backing is easier to manage than “wildcat” moves without audits.

My take
I’m optimistic. Tether’s execution track record has never lost its edge, and its channel advantage in emerging markets is a real moat. As long as BTC holds above $64,230, the stablecoin narrative still has room to ferment; with ETH at $1,899, as long as it doesn’t break down effectively, the DeFi side could also capture some of that premium. Risk point: AI tool rollout takes time—don’t expect a stock-price-style surge in the short term. This is a medium-term narrative, not an overnight catalyst.

- Coins: BTC / BNB
- Direction: Bullish 📈 Expected to rise

title: 🏦 BTC ETF结束“三连流出”，单日回流1.37亿美元：这次带头的不是贝莱德，而是富达
subTitle:
今天机构资金这条线，出现了一个比较明显的变化。
根据 Farside Investors 截至 8月18日 更新的数据，美国现货比特币 ETF 在 8月17日美国交易日 合计录得约 1.373亿美元净流入，结束了此前连续3个交易日的净流出。当天资金主要来自富达 FBTC，净流入约1.119亿美元；ARK 21Shares 的 ARKB约流入1420万美元，Morgan Stanley 的 MSBT约流入1120万美元。
这个反转值得看，但别急着把它理解成：
“机构全面回来了，BTC马上要起飞。”
因为往前看，8月12日、13日、14日三天BTC ETF分别净流出约 6110万、1.311亿和5620万美元，累计约 2.48亿美元。换句话说，8月17日这1.37亿美元回流，虽然明显改善了资金情绪，但还没有完全补回前面三天流出去的钱。
ETH这边就安静得多。
8月17日美国现货ETH ETF合计只有约 500万美元净流入，其中富达 FETH约430万美元、Bitwise ETHW约70万美元。从当天资金强度来看，传统资金明显更偏向BTC，而不是ETH。
有个细节也要注意：Farside目前对8月17日贝莱德 IBIT 一栏显示为“-”，所以这里不要直接解读成“贝莱德零流入”或“贝莱德在撤退”，等数据完整更新再判断更稳妥。
前几天机构踩了刹车，昨天重新踩了一脚油门，但还不能确认已经重新进入持续买入状态。
真正值得盯的是接下来2—3个交易日：

Iran negotiation window closes, missile production increases; it may be hard for BTC to dodge the safe-haven selloff

The US-Iran diplomatic window has closed, Iran has expanded missile production, and safe-haven sentiment is heating up—BTC is under pressure in the short term.

Iran is boosting missile output, while the US side is also upgrading military preparations. Put simply, both sides are stepping up in the direction of “talks going nowhere,” and the window for a diplomatic resolution is basically shut. Source: Crypto Briefing. The key point is this: instability risk in the Middle East is rising. Escalation of geopolitical conflicts has never been good news for risk assets; since crypto is a high-volatility asset, it’s often the first to be sold off for cash.

One-sentence translation: Money is starting to run to safer places, and BTC—an inherently risky asset—may take a cut in the near term.

Market impact
- Short term: Geopolitical conflict escalates → safe-haven sentiment rises → funds flow from risk assets into gold and the US dollar → increased selling pressure on BTC. The transmission path is very direct: as the Middle East situation worsens, institutions first de-leverage; the derivatives market takes the first hit, and spot then follows with downward pressure. BTC is currently at $64,218; it’s only up 1.02% over the past 24 hours, and this safe-haven wave may likely wipe out those gains. ETH at $1,896 has been weak to begin with; it’s down 0.39% in 24 hours and can’t really hold up either.
- Medium term: If the conflict truly breaks out, oil prices rise → inflation expectations increase → the room for the Fed to cut rates gets squeezed → liquidity expectations worsen; that’s a double squeeze on crypto. Unless the situation cools quickly, the rebound’s height is likely limited.

My take
Clearly bearish for the short term. BTC at this level is awkward: above $64,218 there isn’t an obvious buy-side narrative, and with geopolitical headwinds turning negative, it can easily pull back to the $62K support area. ETH is weaker; a break below $1,880 could accelerate the downside. Only if news emerges that both sides are back at the negotiating table will risk appetite repair quickly. Until then, don’t expect too much from any rebound. If you’re holding, focus on leverage ratio—when volatility spikes, leveraged longs that get liquidated often suffer more than the news itself.
